title: 1986 AHSME Problem 28
statement: \(ABCDE\) is a regular pentagon. \(AP,\) \(AQ\) and \(AR\) are the perpendiculars dropped from \(A\) onto \(CD,\) \(CB\) extended and \(DE\) extended, respectively. Let \(O\) be the center of the pentagon. If \(OP=1,\) then \(AO+AQ+AR\) equals

solutions.text:
Let the side length be \(s.\) Since the apothem \(OP=1,\) the five central triangles give pentagon area \(\frac{5s}{2}.\) The same pentagon is the union of triangles \(ABC,\) \(ACD\) and \(ADE,\) whose respective altitudes to side-length bases are \(AQ,AP,AR.\) Hence \[ \frac{s}{2}(AQ+AP+AR)=\frac{5s}{2}, \] so \(AQ+AP+AR=5.\) Also \(AP=AO+OP=AO+1.\) Therefore \(AO+AQ+AR=4.\)

Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: Let \(s\) be the side length and compute the pentagon’s area from its five central triangles
Also split the pentagon into triangles \(ABC,\) \(ACD\) and \(ADE\) with altitudes \(AQ,AP,AR\)
